solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Marry in church after brief separation

indicators.note: the church abbreviation comes after the shortened separation word
a brief word is cut short, so the word for separation loses its last letter

parts.note: a split is a parting or separation
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A couple wed in church after a short time apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To splice is an informal verb for joining two people in wedlock.

clue.text: Remove secondary plot

parts.note: sub- describes something subordinate or secondary, as in a sub-plot
a tract is a plot or stretch of land

explanation.surface: A writer cuts out a subplot from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secondary plot' reads as a subplot to be cut; in fact it supplies both pieces of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to take away or deduct, so it is a synonym of remove.

clue.text: Citizen cutting flower, with permission

indicators.note: the citizen abbreviation cuts into the flower, sitting inside it

parts.note: the lily is a flower
CIT is a short form of citizen

explanation.surface: A townsman picks a bloom, having been allowed to.
explanation.definitionFit: Licitly means lawfully or in a permitted way, the adverb from licit.

clue.text: Host's invitation to wake?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a host says asking someone to visit their home
second meaning: to regain consciousness after fainting

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a host inviting people to a wake, a funeral gathering; instead the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to pay a visit at someone's invitation and to recover consciousness.

clue.text: Order in force to take off cycle race

definitions.text: Order in force to take off
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the air force command sending fighter pilots aloft in a hurry
second meaning: a motorcycle race over rough country

explanation.walkthrough: The 'force' is an air force, whose pilots were ordered to scramble during the Battle of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a fighter squadron's urgent takeoff command and an off-road motorcycle competition.

clue.text: Head of department in hostel's chalet abroad took charge

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered all over, so the letters are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the department word supplies just its opening letter
taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A department manager staying in a chalet hostel overseas was the one in command.
explanation.definitionFit: To call the shots is an idiom for being in control and making the decisions.

clue.text: Parched, drinking cold bitter

indicators.note: the word for parched takes in the cold abbreviation as if swallowing it

parts.note: arid means very dry, parched

explanation.surface: Someone very thirsty downs a chilled pint of bitter beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter looks like the beer being drunk, but it is the definition as an adjective. Bitter is a British pale ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid describes a sharp, pungent, unpleasant taste or smell, a synonym of bitter.

clue.text: Short post from poet circling round lakes

indicators.note: the poet word goes around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a bard is a poet
O is round in shape
L is the map abbreviation for lake, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A low post is taken from a poet who wrote about walking around the lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bollard is a short thick post, used to keep traffic out or moor a ship.

clue.text: Cut out for duty

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to remove by cutting
second meaning: as a noun, a tax charged on goods made at home

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone suited for duty; the two words are a verb and a noun with the same spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for surgically removing something and the noun for a tax on goods.

clue.text: Show particular interest in running order for assembly

parts.note: a production is a staged show
one's line is one's particular field or area of interest

explanation.surface: Someone shows a keen interest in a running order for a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A production line is the sequence of workers and machines through which a product is put together in a factory.

clue.text: Sort of parliamentary form from America mislaid in British Library

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits inside the library abbreviation

parts.note: BL is the abbreviation for the British Library in London

indicators.note: mislaid suggests something put down in the wrong place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A book on American government has been lost in the British Library.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicameral legislature has two chambers, like Congress or Parliament.

clue.text: Catholic priest's into outdated belief?

indicators.note: the priest goes into the Catholic abbreviation

parts.note: RC is Roman Catholic
Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest is keen on an old-fashioned doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' in the surface means keen on; in the wordplay it places one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a survival from the past, such as a custom or idea that has outlived its time.

clue.text: Went to bed weary again?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: went to sleep for the night
second meaning: tired a second time

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, splitting the word as re- plus tired.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring for the night is a formal way of going to sleep, and the split form means made weary anew.

clue.text: Standing objects bordering route

indicators.note: the objects word lies on both sides of the route word, enclosing it

parts.note: ends are aims or objects, as in ends and means
a way is a route

explanation.surface: Upright items line a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Endways means with the end upwards, so something endways is upright, on its end.

clue.text: Turned up tailing shy rodent

indicators.note: tailing means following behind, so this piece goes after the shy word

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful

indicators.note: turned round, the little word up is read backwards

parts.note: the word up itself, taken as written before it is turned

explanation.surface: A timid rodent appeared, following someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American water rodent, also called nutria.

clue.text: Humorous aspect of Spooner's nature affecting all Oxford?

indicators.note: Spooner, an Oxford don, swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds trade places

parts.note: witty means humorous
a side is an aspect

explanation.surface: A funny side of the famous Oxford don's character affects the whole university city.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner swaps the opening sounds: witty side is heard as sitty wide, said like city-wide, so the S sound is written with a C. William Spooner was Warden of New College, Oxford, which is why Oxford fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something citywide extends over a whole city, here the whole of Oxford.

clue.text: Dirty pots, etc, being cast ashore by tide

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the used crockery and pans waiting to be washed after a meal
second meaning: being carried up onto a beach by the sea

explanation.walkthrough: Washing-up is the British term for dirty dishes waiting to be cleaned, or the job of cleaning them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a heap of soiled dishes and things carried up onto the shore by the waves.

clue.text: Force US agents in desert to break up

indicators.note: the agents go inside the desert word

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray one's side
G-men are FBI agents

explanation.surface: American agents in the desert are forced to split up.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert looks like a noun, a sandy place, but it is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To fragment is a verb meaning to shatter into small pieces.

clue.text: Wild forest dwellers rattled medic attending court

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so these pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: to woo is to court a lover

indicators.note: rattled means shaken up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A flustered doctor goes to a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood mice are small wild rodents that live in woodland and fields.

clue.text: Copious work mostly contributed

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the work word loses its last letter

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially of music
lent means gave or contributed, as in lent support

explanation.surface: A great deal of the work was supplied by others.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means lavish and abundant, a synonym of copious.

clue.text: Is a fermented extract less harmful?

indicators.note: an extract is a part taken from a whole, so the letters run inside these words

parts.note: the answer runs across these words, from the end of a through the start of fermented

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fermented extract is healthier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract' looks like a food product in the surface but tells the solver to take letters from the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Safer is the comparative of safe, meaning presenting less danger.

clue.text: Ship's doctor featured in final issue

indicators.note: the doctor word is featured within the final-issue word, inside it

parts.note: fate is the final outcome or destiny
to doctor or rig is to falsify, as with results

explanation.surface: A ship's medical officer is written up in the last edition of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor reads as the ship's physician but is a verb meaning to tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a type of warship.

clue.text: Given a bell polished under pressure

indicators.note: in this down clue the polished word sits under the pressure abbreviation

parts.note: honed means sharpened or polished

explanation.surface: A shiny bell was handed over under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: To give someone a bell is British slang for calling them on the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoned means rang someone, which is what giving someone a bell means in informal British speech.

clue.text: American dons in demand running space centre

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the in-demand word wears the American one inside it

parts.note: hot means popular, in demand
US is the United States
on means operating, running

explanation.surface: American academics are much sought after in running a space centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Dons look like university teachers but are a verb meaning puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: Houston, Texas, is home to NASA's Johnson Space Center, which controls crewed missions.

clue.text: Soviet agency netting a thousand in duties

indicators.note: the agency word catches the thousand inside it like a net

parts.note: TASS was the Soviet news agency
K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A Soviet agency catching a thousand people evading taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are jobs or assignments, a synonym of duties.

clue.text: Attracting attention of husband in a bad way

parts.note: ailing means unwell, in a bad way

explanation.surface: A wife calls out to her husband, who is in a bad way.
explanation.definitionFit: Hailing someone means calling or waving to get their attention, as with a taxi.

clue.text: Calls for CID officer, having first called earlier

indicators.note: the called-earlier word comes first, before the officer

parts.note: née marks a woman's earlier surname, the name she was called before marriage
DS is a Detective Sergeant in the CID, the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: Someone sends for a detective, having phoned beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs is a verb meaning requires, a synonym of calls for.

clue.text: With edges trimmed, season mince and blend

indicators.note: with both edges trimmed off, the season word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: winter is a season
to grate is to shred food finely, much as mincing does

explanation.surface: A cook trims fat, seasons the mince and mixes it all together.
explanation.walkthrough: Season looks like a cooking verb; it is the noun, a time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to combine parts into a whole, a synonym of blend.

clue.text: Reflective journalist subjected to ordeal couldn't stand

indicators.note: reflective means showing a mirror image, so the journalist abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor
tested means put through a trial

explanation.surface: A thoughtful reporter put through a trial couldn't bear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Detested means hated or loathed, which is what couldn't stand means.

clue.text: Finished prescribed course feeling positive

parts.note: up means over or finished, as in time's up
a beat is the set route patrolled by a police officer

explanation.surface: Someone who has completed a prescribed course of medicine feels optimistic.
explanation.walkthrough: Prescribed course suggests medicine; it is a police officer's beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means cheerful and optimistic.
